title: Beyond Base Model Ceilings: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR for Genuinely Novel Reasoning Acquisition
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning coverage, while distillation can introduce genuinely new reasoning patterns. This raises a critical question: can we combine distillation's capacity to expand reasoning boundaries with RL's ability to optimize for correctness, creating a synergistic training paradigm that transcends both approaches individually? Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), a two-phase curriculum. Phase 1 applies targeted distillation from a stronger teacher model specifically on problems where the base model has near-zero pass@k coverage (identified via large-k sampling), injecting genuinely novel reasoning patterns into the student. Phase 2 applies RLVR exclusively on these newly-acquired capabilities, consolidating and refining them through reward-based optimization. A dynamic difficulty scheduler continuously identifies the 'capability frontier' and redirects both phases toward unsolved problems. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using the same pass@k framework from the anchor paper. We compare against RLVR-only, distillation-only, and naive combination baselines across Qwen2.5 and LLaMA3 model families, measuring whether DB-RLVR raises the pass@k ceiling beyond the base model rather than merely improving pass@1 efficiency.

title: Distillation-Augmented RLVR: Injecting Novel Reasoning Patterns Before Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR cannot generate reasoning patterns beyond the base model's latent capability, while distillation genuinely expands reasoning coverage. This raises a natural question: can we combine distillation's pattern-expansion with RLVR's selection/refinement in a principled pipeline to exceed both methods individually?

Proposed Method: We propose a two-stage training paradigm called DA-RLVR. Stage 1 applies targeted distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) specifically on problem types where the base model's pass@large-k coverage is lowest, expanding the model's latent reasoning space. Stage 2 applies RLVR (GRPO/PPO with verifiable rewards) to the distillation-augmented model, allowing RL to select and reinforce the newly injected patterns. We also introduce a 'coverage-guided reward shaping' mechanism that penalizes outputs already well-covered in the base model's distribution, pushing RL to exploit newly distilled patterns rather than revert to pre-existing ones.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k for k∈{1,4,16,64,256}. We compare: (1) base model, (2) pure RLVR, (3) pure distillation, (4) DA-RLVR without coverage shaping, (5) DA-RLVR full. Coverage analysis and perplexity probing verify whether new reasoning patterns persist post-RL.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Reasoning Boundaries as Stepping Stones for Genuine RL Exploration
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by base model coverage while distillation genuinely expands reasoning boundaries. However, distillation alone is limited by teacher quality. A natural question arises: can we combine both—use distillation to first expand the reasoning frontier, then apply RLVR on this stronger initialization to explore beyond even the teacher's boundaries?

Proposed Method: We introduce a two-phase training pipeline. Phase 1: distill from a powerful teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) into a student, expanding its solution coverage. Phase 2: apply RLVR starting from the distilled checkpoint rather than the original base model. We hypothesize that the expanded coverage from distillation provides RLVR a richer exploration landscape, potentially allowing RL to discover solutions neither the original base model nor the teacher can reliably produce. We additionally explore iterative cycling between distillation and RLVR phases.

Experiments: We evaluate pass@k (varying k from 1 to 256) on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks across Qwen2.5 and LLaMA-3 families. We measure coverage expansion relative to base model, distilled model, and teacher at each phase. Ablations test phase ordering, number of cycles, and teacher strength. Primary metric is whether Phase 2 RLVR surpasses the distilled checkpoint's pass@k ceiling, indicating genuine novel reasoning emergence.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Reasoning Boundaries as Targets for Reinforcement Learning
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely expands capabilities by introducing novel reasoning patterns from a teacher. A natural question follows: can we combine both approaches so that RL operates on an already-expanded reasoning space, escaping the base model's ceiling? Proposed Method: We introduce a two-phase pipeline. Phase 1 applies knowledge distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1) to a smaller base model, specifically targeting reasoning traces that lie outside the base model's pass@k coverage—what we call 'frontier traces.' Phase 2 then applies RLVR (e.g., GRPO) starting from this distilled checkpoint, hypothesizing that the expanded coverage from distillation provides new exploration territory for RL to reinforce and generalize. We further propose a curriculum reward shaping that up-weights verifiable problems where the distilled model succeeds but inconsistently (low pass@k), encouraging RL to stabilize newly acquired reasoning patterns. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista using both pass@1 and pass@k (k up to 256). Ablations isolate contributions of each phase, distillation data selection strategy, and reward curriculum. Baselines include standalone distillation, standalone RLVR, and naive sequential combination.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Multi-Turn Environment Interaction as a Path to Novel Reasoning in RLVR
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that single-turn RLVR is bounded by base model coverage—it refines selection over existing reasoning patterns but cannot generate genuinely new ones. We hypothesize this ceiling arises because single-turn rollouts lack the iterative error-correction feedback necessary to compose sub-skills into novel reasoning chains. Proposed Method: We design a multi-turn RL framework where LLMs interact with structured reasoning environments (symbolic math solvers, code interpreters, knowledge graphs) across sequential turns. At each turn, the model receives partial feedback signals—intermediate verification, counterexamples, or partial credit—enabling the model to explore compositional reasoning paths not expressible in a single forward pass. We introduce a 'reasoning novelty reward' that explicitly incentivizes solutions absent from the base model's top-k generations, operationalized via perplexity thresholding against the frozen base model. Planned Experiments: (1) Measure pass@k coverage curves comparing single-turn RLVR, multi-turn RLVR, and distillation baselines on MATH500, AIME, and LiveCodeBench. (2) Ablate turn depth (1, 3, 5, 10 turns) against coverage gain over base model. (3) Analyze whether multi-turn training produces solutions below base model perplexity thresholds, quantifying genuinely novel reasoning patterns. (4) Evaluate cross-domain transfer of acquired reasoning skills to held-out benchmarks.

title: Reasoning Boundary Expansion via Hybrid Distillation-RL: Combining Teacher Knowledge Injection with Verifiable Reward Optimization
description:
Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR merely reshapes sampling distributions within base model capability boundaries, while distillation genuinely expands reasoning coverage by injecting novel teacher patterns. Yet distillation alone lacks online self-improvement and can suffer from teacher error propagation. Can a principled hybrid approach combine distillation's boundary expansion with RL's precision optimization to surpass either method alone?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), a two-phase curriculum. Phase 1 performs targeted distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) specifically on problems where the student base model has zero pass@k coverage, explicitly expanding the capability boundary. Phase 2 applies RLVR with verifiable rewards on the augmented model, optimizing sampling efficiency within the now-expanded boundary. We introduce a 'boundary-aware' replay buffer that prioritizes problems near coverage frontiers, preventing regression on newly acquired patterns.

Experiments: Using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B as base models, we evaluate pass@k (k=1,16,256) on MATH500, AIME2024, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista. We compare against pure RLVR baselines, pure distillation, and naive sequential combinations. Ablations examine Phase 1 data selection strategies (coverage-zero vs. random) and Phase 2 curriculum ordering. Success is measured by whether DB-RLVR achieves pass@256 beyond the base model ceiling identified in the anchor paper.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Expanding the Reasoning Frontier by First Importing Then Reinforcing Novel Patterns
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's latent reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely expands it. Yet pure distillation sacrifices verifiable correctness and can introduce teacher errors. A natural question is: can we combine both—first use distillation to inject new reasoning patterns beyond the base model, then apply RLVR to verify and consolidate them? Proposed Method: We introduce a two-stage pipeline. Stage 1 (Expand): Distill from a stronger teacher model (e.g., DeepSeek-R1) to a smaller base, specifically targeting problem types where pass@k analysis reveals low coverage in the base. Stage 2 (Reinforce): Apply RLVR on the distilled model using verifiable rewards, now operating over an expanded reasoning frontier. We further propose a 'coverage-aware replay' mechanism that periodically samples hard problems where the stage-1 model still underperforms to focus RLVR exploration. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista across 7B/14B model families. Key metrics include pass@k for large k (coverage), pass@1 (precision), and a novel 'new pattern rate' measuring reasoning trajectories absent from the base model. We ablate distillation temperature, teacher choice, and RL algorithm. We hypothesize this pipeline substantially outperforms RLVR-alone and distillation-alone baselines on both coverage and pass@1.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Coverage to Break Base Model Reasoning Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by base model reasoning coverage, while distillation can genuinely expand it by importing teacher reasoning patterns. This raises a natural question: can we combine both — using distillation to first escape the base model's coverage ceiling, then applying RLVR to optimize within the expanded space? Proposed Method: We introduce a two-phase training pipeline. Phase 1 performs targeted distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) focusing specifically on problem types where base model pass@k saturates below 100%, injecting genuinely novel reasoning chains. Phase 2 applies RLVR (GRPO/PPO with verifiable rewards) initialized from the distilled checkpoint. Crucially, we add a 'novelty reward' that explicitly incentivizes solutions not present in the base model's generation distribution, measured via embedding-based diversity from base model rollouts. This prevents RLVR from collapsing back to base model patterns. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks. Primary metric is pass@k across k=1 to k=100. We measure coverage expansion relative to base model, compare against distillation-only and RLVR-only baselines, and ablate the novelty reward coefficient. Success criterion: Phase 2 RLVR improves pass@1 without reducing pass@k relative to Phase 1 distilled model.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Iterative Distillation-RL Loops for Genuinely Novel Reasoning Acquisition
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR is bounded by base model coverage—it reshapes output distributions but cannot introduce reasoning patterns absent from the base model's latent space. Distillation, conversely, can inject genuinely new capabilities from stronger teachers. However, distillation is static: once a student learns from a fixed teacher, further improvement requires a better teacher. We propose a dynamic interleaving framework, DistRL-Loop, that alternates between distillation phases (expanding the model's reasoning frontier by learning from a stronger oracle) and RLVR phases (consolidating and reinforcing newly acquired patterns via verifiable reward signals). Method: Starting from a base model, we (1) distill from a stronger teacher on hard problems the base model cannot solve, (2) apply RLVR to stabilize and generalize the newly acquired skills, then (3) use the improved model as a self-distillation teacher for the next iteration. We introduce a 'novelty coverage' metric tracking how much pass@k improvement comes from patterns absent in the original base model. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and ARC-AGI across 7B/14B models, measuring pass@k curves at each loop iteration, novelty coverage growth, and comparing against pure RLVR, pure distillation, and sequential (distill-then-RLVR) baselines. We hypothesize that DistRL-Loop achieves superlinear coverage expansion beyond any single-phase approach.

title: Iterative Self-Distillation with RLVR: Breaking the Base Model Ceiling Through Teacher-Student Bootstrapping
description:
Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR is fundamentally bounded by the base model's reasoning coverage, while distillation can genuinely expand capabilities by injecting novel reasoning patterns from a stronger teacher. This raises a critical question: can we escape the base model ceiling without requiring an external, fixed teacher model?

Proposed Method: We propose Iterative Self-Distillation with Verifiable Rewards (ISDVR), a bootstrapping framework that alternates between two phases. In Phase 1, an RLVR-trained model generates high-pass@k solutions using diverse sampling, selects correct solutions that differ structurally from the base model's typical reasoning patterns (measured via perplexity under the base model), and constructs a distillation dataset of these 'novel' correct solutions. In Phase 2, the model is fine-tuned via supervised distillation on this dataset, internalizing new reasoning patterns and raising the effective ceiling. These phases alternate over multiple rounds, with the model progressively self-improving beyond its original base.

Experiments: (1) Compare pass@k curves at large k across iterations versus static RLVR baselines; (2) Measure coverage expansion per round on MATH, AIME, and LiveCodeBench; (3) Ablate the novelty-selection criterion (perplexity threshold, structural diversity); (4) Compare against external teacher distillation to quantify the gap; (5) Track reasoning pattern diversity using embedding-based clustering across rounds.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Using Teacher Coverage Gaps to Seed Genuinely Novel Reasoning in Student Models
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR cannot exceed base model reasoning coverage (pass@k ceiling), while distillation genuinely expands it by importing teacher reasoning patterns. However, pure distillation is costly and the teacher's patterns may not generalize optimally for the student. Can we combine both approaches synergistically—using distillation specifically to inject reasoning patterns absent from the base model, then applying RLVR to consolidate and extend them? Method: We propose Coverage-Guided Hybrid Training (CGHT). First, we identify 'coverage gaps'—problems where the base model fails at large k but the teacher succeeds—using efficient pass@k estimation. We then perform targeted distillation exclusively on these gap problems, transplanting novel reasoning chains into the student. Second, we apply RLVR on the distillation-augmented model to reinforce correct patterns and improve pass@1 efficiency. We introduce a curriculum that gradually shifts from distillation loss to RL reward as coverage improves, preventing catastrophic forgetting of transplanted patterns. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks across Qwen and LLaMA families. Metrics include pass@1, pass@k (k=16,64,256), coverage, and perplexity. Ablations isolate contribution of gap-targeted vs. random distillation and the sequencing of distillation vs. RL phases.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Curiosity-Driven Exploration to Push RLVR Beyond Base Model Coverage Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR-trained models are bounded by base model coverage—they improve selection efficiency (low k) but cannot generate reasoning patterns absent from the base model's distribution. This suggests current RLVR suffers from pure exploitation of existing capabilities rather than genuine exploration of novel reasoning strategies. Proposed Method: We introduce Curiosity-Augmented RLVR (CA-RLVR), which augments standard verifiable-reward RL with an intrinsic curiosity reward that explicitly incentivizes generating reasoning trajectories with low base-model likelihood (high perplexity under the frozen base). Specifically, the total reward combines task correctness with a novelty bonus proportional to the KL divergence between the current policy's trajectory distribution and the base model's, constrained to avoid incoherence via a fluency filter. This directly targets the coverage gap identified in the anchor paper by rewarding the model for discovering correct solutions the base model would rarely generate. Experiments: We evaluate CA-RLVR on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning tasks using the same pass@k framework from the anchor paper, measuring whether training expands coverage beyond base model pass@k ceilings. Ablations isolate the curiosity bonus magnitude, fluency constraint thresholds, and interaction with different base models (Qwen2.5, Llama3). Success criterion: CA-RLVR trained models exceed base model pass@k at large k values on held-out problems.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding Base Model Reasoning Boundaries via Diversity-Aware RLVR
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR fails to elicit genuinely novel reasoning patterns beyond those latent in the base model—the base model's pass@k at large k upper-bounds RLVR-trained models. This suggests current reward signals optimize for mode-seeking (high-probability correct paths) rather than coverage expansion. We hypothesize that rewarding novel reasoning trajectories not previously sampled from the base model could push beyond this ceiling.

Method: We propose Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), augmenting standard verifiable rewards with a diversity bonus that incentivizes solution paths absent from a fixed reference set of base model rollouts. Specifically, for each training problem we pre-collect N base model solutions, embed them using intermediate hidden states, and construct a coverage map. During RL training, the reward combines correctness verification with a novelty score—measured as distance from the base model's solution manifold in embedding space—subject to a correctness gate to avoid rewarding wrong-but-novel paths.

Experiments: (1) Compare pass@k curves (k=1 to 256) of CG-RLVR vs. standard RLVR vs. base model on MATH, AIME, and LiveCodeBench; (2) Measure coverage expansion relative to base model rollouts; (3) Ablate novelty weight and reference set size; (4) Compare against distillation baselines from the anchor paper to assess whether CG-RLVR approaches distillation's coverage gains without requiring a teacher model.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Iterative Distillation-RL Loops for Genuinely Novel Reasoning Acquisition
description: Problem: The anchor paper establishes that RLVR is bounded by base model coverage—it exploits existing reasoning patterns rather than discovering new ones, while distillation genuinely expands capabilities. This raises the question: can we systematically break the base model ceiling by alternating distillation and RL in a principled loop? Proposed Method: We introduce IterDRL, an iterative framework that cycles between (1) distillation phases, where the model learns from a stronger teacher (e.g., GPT-4o or a frontier model) on problems the current model cannot solve at any k, and (2) RLVR consolidation phases, which stabilize and generalize the newly acquired patterns via verifiable reward signals. Crucially, after each distillation phase, we re-measure the pass@k boundary to identify which problems remain outside coverage, targeting those specifically in the next distillation step. This creates a directed capability expansion loop rather than random knowledge transfer. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and a novel visual reasoning suite across 7B and 14B models. We track pass@k curves, coverage growth, and perplexity of novel solution types across iterations, comparing against pure RLVR, single-shot distillation, and distillation-only baselines. We also measure compute efficiency (new capabilities per FLOP) to assess practical viability.

title: Coverage-Guided Exploration Bonuses for RLVR: Breaking the Base Model Ceiling Through Deliberate Reasoning Diversity
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by base model coverage—it improves pass@1 but fails to expand the reasoning frontier (pass@large-k). Current RLVR reward signals only reinforce correctness, ignoring diversity of reasoning paths, causing the policy to collapse onto high-probability base model solutions rather than exploring latent capabilities. Proposed Method: We introduce Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), augmenting the verifiable reward with an intrinsic diversity bonus that explicitly incentivizes novel reasoning trajectories. Specifically, we maintain a dynamic embedding store of previously generated solution chains and reward solutions whose chain-of-thought embeddings are distant from existing clusters (novelty reward via approximate nearest-neighbor distance). Additionally, we apply a perplexity-weighted sampling curriculum that preferentially trains on problems where base model solution diversity is low, forcing exploration in underrepresented reasoning regions. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning (MathVista) using the same pass@k methodology as the anchor paper (k up to 256). We compare CG-RLVR against standard GRPO/PPO baselines and distillation, measuring both pass@1 (exploitation) and pass@large-k (exploration/coverage). We track embedding space coverage growth across training to verify genuine reasoning expansion beyond base model boundaries.

title: Expanding the Reasoning Frontier: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR for Genuinely Novel Capability Acquisition
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR is bounded by the base model's latent capabilities (pass@k ceiling), while distillation genuinely expands reasoning by introducing teacher patterns. However, distillation alone is limited by the teacher's fixed distribution. Can we design a training paradigm that iteratively uses distillation to break the base model's ceiling, then applies RLVR to consolidate and explore further, creating a compounding capability expansion loop?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), an alternating training scheme: (1) Distillation Phase — use a stronger teacher to inject novel reasoning trajectories that lie outside the student base model's pass@k coverage; (2) RLVR Phase — apply verifiable reward RL starting from the distillation-expanded checkpoint to consolidate and selectively amplify correct novel patterns; (3) Repeat with progressively harder problems. Crucially, we use pass@k coverage at large k as the primary diagnostic to verify each phase genuinely expands the frontier rather than merely shifting probability mass.

Experiments: We apply DB-RLVR to Qwen2.5-7B/14B on MATH500, AIME, and LiveCodeBench. We measure pass@k (k up to 256), coverage growth per cycle, and out-of-distribution generalization to novel problem types unseen during distillation, comparing against pure RLVR, pure distillation, and naive sequential baselines.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Distillation-Seeded Exploration to Break the Base Model Reasoning Ceiling in RLVR
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR-trained models are bounded by their base model's reasoning coverage (pass@large-k), while distillation genuinely expands capabilities by importing novel reasoning patterns. This raises a concrete question: can distillation be used strategically as an initialization or exploration mechanism within RL training to help models escape the base model ceiling?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Seeded Reinforcement Learning (DSRL), a curriculum that interleaves two phases. First, targeted distillation from a stronger teacher injects reasoning traces that fall outside the base model's coverage (identified via pass@k gap analysis). Second, RLVR fine-tuning with entropy-regularized policy optimization is applied from this expanded initialization, explicitly rewarding solutions that are low-probability under the original base model but verifiably correct. We use KL divergence from the base model as a diversity bonus alongside task reward, incentivizing genuine novelty rather than redistribution of existing patterns.

Experiments: (1) Measure pass@k (k up to 256) across math (MATH500, AIME), coding (HumanEval+), and visual reasoning benchmarks, comparing DSRL against vanilla RLVR, pure distillation, and base models. (2) Track coverage expansion over training using perplexity-under-base-model as a proxy for novelty. (3) Ablate distillation curriculum difficulty and KL bonus coefficient. We hypothesize DSRL meaningfully surpasses the base model ceiling measured by pass@large-k.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Expanding Reasoning Boundaries by Seeding Novel Patterns Before Policy Optimization
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's latent reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely expands it. Yet pure distillation lacks the self-improvement dynamics of RL. Can we combine them to get both expansion and optimization? Proposed Method: We introduce a two-phase training pipeline called Seed-then-Refine (STR). Phase 1 applies targeted distillation from a stronger teacher specifically on problems where the base model's pass@k (large k) is near zero—i.e., problems outside the base model's coverage boundary. This seeds genuinely novel reasoning patterns. Phase 2 applies RLVR starting from the distilled checkpoint, now with an expanded coverage ceiling, allowing RL to optimize within a broader capability space. We include a coverage-aware curriculum that continuously identifies and prioritizes problems still near the model's coverage boundary during RL training. Experiments: We evaluate STR across math (MATH-500, AMC/AIME), coding (HumanEval+, LiveCodeBench), and visual reasoning (MathVista) benchmarks using both pass@1 (sampling efficiency) and pass@k at large k (coverage expansion). Baselines include pure RLVR, pure distillation, sequential distillation+RLVR without curriculum, and RLVR from the base model. We measure coverage boundary shift, perplexity distributions, and sample efficiency to disentangle the contributions of each phase.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR to Genuinely Expand LLM Reasoning Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reshapes the base model's existing reasoning distribution (improving pass@1 at the cost of pass@k coverage), while distillation genuinely introduces new reasoning patterns. This raises a critical question: can we hybridize distillation and RLVR to escape the base model's capability ceiling while retaining RL's self-improvement properties? Proposed Method: We propose Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), a two-phase curriculum. Phase 1 uses targeted distillation from a stronger teacher on specifically those problem types where the student base model has near-zero pass@k coverage (identified via systematic coverage profiling), injecting genuinely novel reasoning patterns into the policy initialization. Phase 2 applies RLVR starting from this distillation-augmented policy, with a coverage-aware reward that explicitly incentivizes the model to solve problems outside its original pass@k support, rather than over-exploiting already-covered solution paths. Planned Experiments: (1) Measure pass@k (k=1,4,16,64,256) on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista before/after each phase; (2) Use coverage and perplexity metrics from the anchor paper to track whether DB-RLVR expands beyond the original base model ceiling; (3) Ablate distillation scope, teacher strength, and coverage-aware reward weighting; (4) Compare against standard RLVR and pure distillation baselines across Qwen2.5 and LLaMA-3 families.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Reasoning Boundaries to Break the Base Model Ceiling
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely expands it. A critical open question is whether combining distillation-derived reasoning patterns with subsequent RL fine-tuning can surpass both approaches alone—creating a virtuous cycle that iteratively pushes the reasoning frontier beyond any single base model. Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), a staged pipeline: (1) perform targeted reasoning distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) to inject novel reasoning patterns into a smaller base model, producing an enriched 'seed' model; (2) apply RLVR on the seed model using verifiable rewards, exploiting the expanded coverage as a broader exploration space; (3) iterate distillation and RL stages, each time using the current model as the new baseline. We hypothesize that each distillation stage raises the effective ceiling for subsequent RL exploitation. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AMC/AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k (k=1,10,100) and coverage metrics across 7B/13B model families. Ablations compare: base→RLVR, base→distill, base→distill→RLVR, and multiple DB-RLVR iterations. We track whether each stage genuinely introduces new solution trajectories via perplexity and n-gram novelty analysis versus base model outputs.

title: Boundary-Aware RLVR: Dynamically Estimating and Pushing the Base Model Reasoning Ceiling via Adaptive Exploration Bonuses
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR-trained models are fundamentally bounded by base model capability (measurable via pass@k at large k), yet current RL algorithms ignore this ceiling during training, wasting compute on problems already solvable and failing to push the boundary on truly hard problems. Method: We propose Boundary-Aware RLVR (BA-RLVR), which continuously estimates the per-problem 'coverage gap' — the difference between base model pass@k (approximated via Monte Carlo sampling) and the current policy's pass@1 — and uses this gap to shape exploration bonuses during RL training. For problems where the base model already achieves high coverage, rewards are discounted to avoid reinforcing superficial formatting gains. For problems near or beyond base model coverage, we apply amplified intrinsic bonuses and curriculum prioritization to force genuine generalization. We additionally introduce a 'boundary-crossing' metric tracking how often the RL policy solves problems the base model never solved across 256 samples. Experiments: We evaluate BA-RLVR against standard GRPO/PPO on Qwen2.5-7B/14B and Llama-3.1-8B across MATH500, AIME2024, LiveCodeBench, and a held-out compositional reasoning suite. Primary metrics include pass@1, pass@k, boundary-crossing rate, and compute efficiency. We hypothesize BA-RLVR significantly increases boundary-crossing rate while maintaining competitive pass@1 gains.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding Base Model Reasoning Boundaries via Diversity-Aware RLVR
description:
Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR merely reweights existing base model reasoning patterns rather than discovering genuinely new ones, with pass@k coverage capping at the base model's ceiling. This suggests current reward signals optimize exploitation of known solutions without incentivizing exploration of novel reasoning trajectories.

Proposed Method: We introduce Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), which augments standard verifiable rewards with an intrinsic diversity bonus. Specifically, we maintain a rolling embedding buffer of previously generated correct reasoning chains. The diversity reward is computed as the maximum cosine distance between a new correct solution's chain-of-thought embedding and all buffered solutions. This encourages the policy to discover structurally distinct correct reasoning paths. We combine this with a 'boundary probing' curriculum that periodically tests whether newly discovered solution patterns extend pass@k coverage beyond the base model's frozen reference distribution, updating training difficulty accordingly.

Experiments: (1) Track pass@k curves (k=1 to 256) for CG-RLVR vs. standard RLVR vs. base models on MATH500, AIME, and HumanEval across Qwen-2.5-Math and DeepSeek-R1 families. (2) Measure solution embedding coverage via convex hull volume in PCA space. (3) Ablate diversity reward weight and buffer size. (4) Compare against distillation baselines from the anchor paper. Success criterion: CG-RLVR pass@k exceeds base model coverage at large k values.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Expanding Reasoning Boundaries by Seeding Novel Patterns Before Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely introduces novel reasoning patterns. However, distilled models may suffer from over-reliance on teacher styles and lack the precision-maximizing benefits of reward-guided optimization. Can we combine these complementary strengths?

Proposed Method: We propose a two-stage training pipeline: (1) Targeted Distillation Seeding — selectively distill only reasoning traces covering problem types where the base model has near-zero pass@k coverage, identified via automated coverage gap analysis; (2) RLVR Consolidation — apply RLVR on the distillation-expanded model to sharpen and stabilize the newly introduced reasoning patterns under verifiable reward signals. We introduce a 'novelty-weighted' reward that gives higher signal for solutions lying outside the original base model's coverage distribution, operationalized via perplexity thresholding relative to the base model.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, CodeContests, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k for k∈{1,4,16,64,256}. Baselines include pure RLVR, pure distillation, naive sequential distillation+RLVR, and the base model. Ablations examine distillation dataset size, novelty-reward thresholds, and coverage gap identification strategies. Success is measured by whether the hybrid model exceeds the base model's pass@large-k upper bound established by the anchor paper.

title: Escape Velocity: Combining Distillation-Seeded Exploration with RLVR to Genuinely Expand Base Model Reasoning Boundaries
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by base model coverage (pass@k at large k), while distillation genuinely introduces new reasoning patterns. Yet distillation requires a stronger teacher, and pure RLVR plateaus. Can we combine both to exceed both the base model ceiling and pure distillation?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Seeded RLVR (DS-RLVR), a two-phase training paradigm. Phase 1: Perform targeted distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) on a small seed set of hard problems where the base model has zero coverage, injecting genuinely novel reasoning chains. Phase 2: Apply RLVR starting from this distilled checkpoint, using a coverage-aware reward that explicitly bonuses solutions that lie outside the original base model's sampled solution distribution (measured via embedding-space novelty relative to base model outputs). Experiments: (1) Pass@k analysis (k up to 256) comparing base model, pure RLVR, pure distillation, and DS-RLVR on MATH-500, AIME 2024-25, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista. title: Escape Velocity: Combining Distillation-Seeded Exploration with RLVR to Surpass Base Model Reasoning Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by base model coverage at large k, while distillation genuinely expands reasoning patterns. Crucially, we introduce a novelty bonus reward that incentivizes solution paths dissimilar to base model rollouts, pushing exploration beyond inherited patterns. title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Curiosity-Driven Exploration in RLVR to Elicit Genuinely Novel Reasoning Patterns
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reshapes the base model's existing reasoning distribution rather than generating fundamentally new capabilities—the base model's pass@k ceiling is never exceeded. This suggests current RLVR suffers from insufficient exploration: reward signals only reinforce already-probable solutions. Proposed Method: We introduce Curiosity-Augmented RLVR (CA-RLVR), which augments verifiable task rewards with an intrinsic curiosity bonus based on reasoning-path novelty. Specifically, we maintain a retrieval index of previously generated chain-of-thought trajectories and compute a novelty score (via embedding distance or n-gram divergence) for each new rollout. This bonus incentivizes the model to explore structurally distinct reasoning strategies beyond high-probability base-model paths. We additionally incorporate a diversity-constrained beam rollout scheme during training to prevent mode collapse. Experiments: (1) We replicate the anchor paper's pass@k coverage analysis across math (MATH500, AMC/AIME), code (HumanEval+), and visual reasoning benchmarks to establish baselines. (2) We train Qwen2.5-7B/32B and Llama-3.1-8B with CA-RLVR and standard RLVR, comparing pass@k curves at large k, coverage growth over training, and perplexity of novel solutions. (3) We measure whether CA-RLVR's discovered solutions genuinely exceed the base model's coverage ceiling, providing the first evidence that exploration-augmented RL can break the identified upper bound.

title: Expanding Reasoning Boundaries via Curriculum-Guided Environment Interaction: A Multi-Turn RLVR Framework
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that current RLVR methods are bounded by base model capabilities, as evidenced by base models achieving higher pass@k at large k. This suggests that single-turn RLVR cannot elicit genuinely novel reasoning patterns. However, multi-turn agent-environment interaction—where the model can query tools, receive feedback, and iteratively refine reasoning—may allow exploration beyond the base model's static distribution.

Proposed Method: We design a multi-turn RLVR framework where LLMs interact with a structured reasoning environment (Python interpreter, symbolic math solver, search engine) across sequential turns. A curriculum scheduler progressively introduces problems where base model coverage (pass@k, large k) is near zero, ensuring training focuses on genuinely out-of-distribution challenges. Rewards combine final answer correctness with intermediate tool-use quality signals. We additionally incorporate a 'novelty bonus' that rewards reasoning trajectories dissimilar to base model high-probability completions, explicitly incentivizing exploration beyond the base distribution.

Experiments: (1) Measure pass@k (k=1,10,100) for base, single-turn RLVR, and our multi-turn framework on MATH-500, LiveCodeBench, and geometry benchmarks. (2) Coverage analysis comparing trajectory distributions against base model. (3) Ablations on curriculum difficulty, novelty bonus weight, and tool availability. Success criterion: multi-turn framework achieves higher pass@100 than base model, demonstrating genuinely expanded reasoning capacity.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Curriculum-Guided Exploration in RLVR via Deliberate Out-of-Distribution Problem Injection
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR-trained models are bounded by their base model's latent reasoning coverage—RLVR merely shifts probability mass toward correct solutions already latent in the base model rather than discovering genuinely novel reasoning strategies. This raises the question: can carefully structured training curricula force exploration beyond this ceiling?

Proposed Method: We introduce Boundary-Seeking RLVR (BS-RLVR), which explicitly targets the base model's capability boundary during training. First, we estimate the base model's reasoning frontier by identifying problems where base model pass@k saturates near zero even at large k (true capability gaps). Second, we construct a dynamic curriculum that progressively injects these 'capability-gap' problems—problems where distillation from a stronger teacher provides sparse but genuine signal—interleaved with standard RLVR training. Third, we add a diversity-promoting entropy bonus calibrated relative to the base model's token distribution to discourage regression to already-mastered reasoning patterns.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, CodeContests, and ARC-AGI using pass@k (k up to 256) as the primary metric. We compare BS-RLVR against standard GRPO/PPO baselines and pure distillation, measuring both capability-gap problem coverage and held-out generalization. Ablations isolate contributions of curriculum scheduling, teacher signal injection, and entropy bonuses. Success is defined as surpassing base model pass@k ceilings on capability-gap problem subsets.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Expanding Reasoning Boundaries by Bootstrapping Novel Patterns Before Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning patterns, while distillation genuinely introduces new ones. Yet distillation alone lacks the self-improvement dynamics of RL. Can we combine both to exceed what either achieves independently?

Proposed Method: We propose a two-stage hybrid training pipeline. Stage 1 (Boundary Expansion): Apply targeted distillation from a stronger teacher model (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) using only problems where the base model fails at large k but the teacher succeeds — precisely the out-of-distribution reasoning patterns the anchor paper identifies as missing. This expands the student's coverage boundary. Stage 2 (Boundary Exploitation): Apply RLVR on top of the distillation-expanded model, now with a richer reasoning repertoire to explore and refine via verifiable rewards. We also introduce a 'novelty bonus' reward signal that explicitly incentivizes solution paths absent in the original base model's output distribution.

Experiments: Evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k for k∈{1,4,16,64,256}. Compare: (1) base model, (2) RLVR only, (3) distillation only, (4) hybrid pipeline. Measure coverage expansion, perplexity on held-out reasoning chains, and benchmark accuracy to quantify whether the hybrid genuinely surpasses base model boundaries.

title: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR: Expanding Then Sharpening Reasoning Boundaries in LLMs
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning coverage, while distillation genuinely expands it. However, distillation alone suffers from teacher-bounded ceiling effects and mode-averaging. This suggests a natural hybrid: first expand the reasoning boundary via distillation, then sharpen selection within the expanded space via RLVR. Method: We propose a two-stage training pipeline called Expand-then-Sharpen (EtS). Stage 1 applies knowledge distillation from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-671B) to inject novel reasoning patterns into the student, explicitly maximizing coverage of the teacher's solution distribution. Stage 2 applies RLVR (e.g., GRPO) starting from this distilled checkpoint, using verifiable rewards to improve precision and reliability within the newly expanded reasoning space. We also investigate intermediate variants: interleaving distillation and RL rounds, and using RL-generated rollouts to select high-quality distillation targets. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using both pass@1 (precision) and pass@k at large k (coverage). Ablations compare stage ordering, dataset mixing ratios, and distillation temperature. We measure whether EtS surpasses both pure distillation and pure RLVR on coverage-precision Pareto frontiers, and analyze whether RL post-distillation creates genuinely novel patterns beyond the teacher.

title: Distillation-Initialized RLVR: Bootstrapping Genuinely Novel Reasoning Before Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning patterns, while distillation genuinely expands reasoning capabilities by introducing novel patterns from a teacher. A natural question arises: can we combine distillation and RLVR synergistically—first using distillation to expand the model's reasoning frontier, then applying RLVR to efficiently select and reinforce those newly acquired patterns? Method: We propose a two-stage pipeline called Distill-then-Reinforce (D2R). Stage 1: distill reasoning traces from a stronger teacher (e.g., DeepSeek-R1) into a smaller base model, explicitly seeding it with novel reasoning patterns beyond its original coverage. Stage 2: apply RLVR on this distilled model, using verifiable rewards to selectively reinforce high-quality reasoning chains. We hypothesize that RLVR on a distillation-expanded model will achieve a higher coverage ceiling than RLVR on the raw base model, since the starting distribution is richer. We also introduce a 'novel pattern utilization rate'—the fraction of RLVR-selected solutions that originate from distillation-introduced patterns—as a diagnostic metric. Experiments: Evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning tasks across Qwen2.5, LLaMA3, and Mistral model families, comparing base→RLVR, base→distill, distill→RLVR, and jointly trained variants using pass@k for large k, coverage analysis, and perplexity decomposition.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Targeted Distillation Bootstrapping to Break the Base Model Ceiling in RLVR
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's reasoning coverage—it cannot discover genuinely novel reasoning patterns. Meanwhile, distillation can inject new patterns but lacks the self-improvement dynamics of RL. Can we combine both to transcend the base model ceiling?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR (DB-RLVR), a two-phase curriculum. Phase 1 identifies 'boundary problems'—problems where the base model has near-zero pass@k coverage but a stronger teacher model succeeds—using the pass@k gap as a difficulty signal. We distill only on these boundary problems to surgically inject novel reasoning patterns into the student. Phase 2 applies RLVR starting from this distillation-augmented checkpoint, using verifiable rewards to reinforce and generalize the newly acquired patterns rather than merely sharpening existing ones. A key novelty is a 'novelty bonus' reward that explicitly incentivizes solution trajectories dissimilar (measured by edit distance on reasoning chains) from the base model's typical outputs.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning (MathVista) using pass@k (k=1,10,100). Baselines include vanilla RLVR, pure distillation, and sequential distillation+RLVR without boundary targeting. Primary metric is whether DB-RLVR surpasses the teacher's pass@k coverage on held-out problems, demonstrating genuine capability expansion beyond both base model and teacher.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Iterative Distillation-RL Loops for Genuinely Novel Reasoning in LLMs
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR fails to elicit reasoning patterns beyond the base model's latent capabilities (bounded by pass@k at large k), while distillation can genuinely expand reasoning. This raises a natural question: can we design a hybrid training paradigm that systematically transcends the base model ceiling by combining distillation's capacity to introduce novel patterns with RL's ability to reinforce and stabilize them? Proposed Method: We introduce Iterative Distillation-RL (IDRL), a cyclical training framework where: (1) a stronger teacher model generates diverse high-quality reasoning traces for problems the student currently fails, expanding the student's coverage beyond its base model ceiling; (2) RLVR then fine-tunes the expanded model to select and reinforce the most reliable newly-acquired patterns; (3) the improved student becomes the next cycle's starting point, enabling progressive ceiling elevation. Crucially, we introduce a 'ceiling elevation metric' — the difference in pass@k (large k) between the current model and its initialization — to quantify genuine reasoning expansion per cycle. Experiments: We test IDRL on Qwen2.5 and Llama3 families across math (MATH500, AIME), coding (HumanEval, LiveCodeBench), and visual reasoning (MathVista) benchmarks, comparing against RLVR-only and one-shot distillation baselines, tracking ceiling elevation across cycles to demonstrate genuine capability expansion.

title: Breaking the Base Model Ceiling: Continual Pretraining and RLVR Co-Training for Genuinely Novel Reasoning Acquisition
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR merely refines existing base model capabilities (improving pass@1) without expanding the coverage ceiling (pass@k for large k). This suggests current RLVR is fundamentally constrained by base model knowledge boundaries. Can we design a training paradigm that simultaneously expands the ceiling while optimizing selection within it?

Proposed Method: We propose CoPRL (Coverage-expanding Pre-training + RL), a co-training framework alternating between: (1) targeted continual pretraining on synthetically generated hard reasoning chains that lie outside the base model's current coverage (identified via high perplexity + failed pass@k problems), and (2) RLVR fine-tuning to improve greedy selection within the expanded distribution. The synthetic data generation uses a stronger teacher model to produce solutions for problems the base model consistently fails, creating genuine coverage expansion similar to distillation but without requiring expensive labeled datasets at scale.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k (k=1,10,100) as the primary metric. Ablations compare: RLVR-only, continual pretraining-only, distillation-only, and CoPRL. We track coverage expansion relative to the original base model ceiling, perplexity on held-out hard problems, and compute efficiency. We test across Qwen-2.5, LLaMA-3, and DeepSeek model families to validate generality.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Distillation-Seeded Exploration to Help RLVR Transcend Base Model Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR-trained models are bounded by base model coverage—they never produce reasoning patterns absent from the base model at large k. Yet distillation genuinely expands coverage. This raises a concrete question: can distillation-generated novel reasoning traces be used as targeted seeds to help RLVR escape base model boundaries? Method: We propose Distillation-Seeded Reinforcement Learning (DSRL), a two-phase curriculum. Phase 1 identifies 'coverage gaps'—problems where the base model fails at pass@100 but a stronger teacher succeeds—and distills teacher traces specifically for these hard problems into the student. Phase 2 applies RLVR starting from the distillation-augmented checkpoint, using the newly acquired reasoning patterns as launching pads for further RL exploration. We introduce a 'novelty reward bonus' that explicitly rewards generating token sequences with low perplexity under the distilled model but high perplexity under the original base model, incentivizing genuine exploration beyond base boundaries. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks across 7B/14B Qwen and LLaMA models, measuring pass@k curves (k up to 256), coverage overlap metrics, and perplexity divergence from base model. We compare against pure RLVR, pure distillation, and naive distillation+RLVR fine-tuning baselines.

title: Escape Velocity: Measuring and Maximizing RLVR's Ability to Exceed Base Model Coverage via Synthetic Environment Diversity
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR-trained models are bounded by base model coverage at large k, suggesting RL merely reshapes the sampling distribution rather than expanding it. But this finding may conflate environment richness with algorithmic limitation—current RLVR uses static, homogeneous problem sets. If the reward environment lacks sufficient diversity and novelty, the policy cannot discover reasoning patterns absent in pretraining data. Proposed Method: We introduce 'Coverage Escape Rate' (CER), a metric quantifying how often RLVR-trained models produce correct solutions on problems whose solutions have near-zero base model pass@k. We then systematically vary environment diversity along three axes: (1) procedurally generated math problems with controllable distributional shift from pretraining, (2) multi-turn interactive proof environments with adversarial hint-withholding, (3) compositional reasoning tasks requiring chaining skills not co-occurring in pretraining corpora. We train with PPO and GRPO across these environments and measure CER alongside standard pass@k. Experiments: Using Qwen-2.5-Math and DeepSeek-R1-Distill as base models, we compare static vs. diverse curricula on AMC/AIME, novel procedural benchmarks, and out-of-distribution compositional tasks. We hypothesize diverse multi-turn environments will produce measurable positive CER, demonstrating a path toward genuine reasoning expansion beyond base model boundaries.

title: Expanding the Reasoning Frontier: Combining Distillation-Seeded Exploration with RLVR to Surpass Base Model Ceilings
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR is bounded by base model coverage — it selectively amplifies existing reasoning patterns rather than discovering novel ones. Distillation, by contrast, genuinely injects new reasoning patterns. Yet distillation alone lacks the self-improvement dynamics of RL. Can we combine distillation's frontier-expanding property with RLVR's refinement to surpass both the base model ceiling and the distillation teacher?

Proposed Method: We introduce Distillation-Seeded RLVR (DS-RLVR), a two-phase pipeline. Phase 1: perform targeted distillation from a stronger teacher only on problems where the base model has zero pass@k coverage (the 'dead zone'), explicitly injecting novel reasoning traces. Phase 2: apply RLVR starting from this distillation-augmented checkpoint, using a curriculum that overweights previously-zero-coverage problems to consolidate and generalize the newly acquired patterns.

Experiments: (1) Measure pass@k coverage before/after each phase across MATH, AIME, CodeContests, and visual reasoning benchmarks. (2) Compare against pure distillation, pure RLVR, and sequential distillation→RLVR without dead-zone targeting. (3) Analyze whether DS-RLVR's pass@1 performance exceeds the teacher on held-out problems, indicating genuine generalization beyond distilled examples. (4) Ablate the dead-zone identification threshold and curriculum weighting strategy.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding RLVR Beyond Base Model Boundaries via Novelty Bonuses
description: Problem: As shown by the anchor paper, RLVR training merely reshapes the sampling distribution of base model capabilities (improving pass@1) without unlocking genuinely new reasoning patterns (bounded by base model pass@k at large k). The fundamental challenge is incentivizing LLMs to explore reasoning paths that lie outside the base model's existing coverage. Proposed Method: We introduce Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), which augments standard verifiable reward signals with a novelty bonus that rewards generation of reasoning trajectories not already covered by the base model. Specifically, we maintain a trajectory embedding store of base model solutions and compute a coverage-based intrinsic reward using kernel density estimation in a learned reasoning embedding space. This bonus decays as trajectories become well-represented in the store, pushing the policy toward structurally novel solution strategies while still optimizing for correctness. We additionally incorporate a diversity regularization term in the policy gradient objective to prevent mode collapse onto a few novel patterns. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks (MathVista) using pass@k across k=1 to k=100 as the primary metric. We compare against six baseline RLVR algorithms from the anchor paper, measuring whether CG-RLVR closes the gap between trained-model pass@1 performance and base-model pass@large-k coverage ceiling, with ablations isolating the novelty bonus and diversity regularization contributions.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding Base Model Reasoning Boundaries via Diversity-Incentivized RLVR
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR merely reweights existing reasoning patterns from the base model rather than discovering genuinely novel ones, as evidenced by base models achieving higher pass@k at large k. This suggests current reward signals (correctness only) fail to push models beyond their prior solution distribution. Proposed Method: We introduce Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), which augments standard verifiable rewards with an explicit diversity bonus that incentivizes the model to produce reasoning trajectories dissimilar from its own rollout history and from base model high-probability paths. Concretely, we maintain a trajectory embedding buffer per problem and compute a coverage reward proportional to the minimum cosine distance of a new rollout from existing buffer entries, weighted inversely by base model perplexity (rewarding solutions the base model finds surprising). This combined reward encourages exploration of low-probability but correct reasoning chains. Experiments: (1) Train Qwen-2.5-Math and DeepSeek-R1-Distill variants with CG-RLVR vs. standard GRPO on MATH500, AMC/AIME, and LiveCodeBench; (2) Evaluate pass@k (k=1,4,16,64,256) to test whether coverage-reward training expands the boundary beyond the base model ceiling identified in the anchor; (3) Perplexity and clustering analyses of generated solutions to verify emergence of genuinely novel reasoning patterns; (4) Ablations isolating diversity bonus weight and buffer size effects.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Reasoning Boundaries to Unlock Genuine RL Self-Improvement
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR is bounded by the base model's existing reasoning patterns, while distillation genuinely expands coverage. This raises a natural question: can distillation be used strategically to first expand the model's reasoning frontier, after which RLVR can then further optimize within this enlarged space—breaking the ceiling that limits pure RLVR?

Phase 1 performs targeted distillation from a stronger teacher model, but only on problem types where the base model's pass@k coverage is near zero (identified via systematic coverage profiling). This injects genuinely novel reasoning patterns for hard problems. Phase 2 applies RLVR on the distilled checkpoint, hypothesizing that the expanded reasoning boundary now allows RL to discover optimization paths unavailable to the original base model. We additionally propose a coverage-guided reward shaping mechanism that explicitly rewards solutions that lie outside the base model's high-probability token trajectories, incentivizing genuine exploration.

Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using pass@k at varying k. Ablations compare: base→RLVR, base→distill, base→distill→RLVR, and base→RLVR→distill. We measure coverage expansion, perplexity relative to base model, and performance at both small and large k to determine whether the sequential approach breaks the RLVR ceiling identified in the anchor paper.

title: Distillation-Bootstrapped RLVR: Using Teacher-Expanded Coverage to Break Base Model Reasoning Ceilings
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR is bounded by base model coverage (pass@k), while distillation genuinely expands reasoning capabilities by introducing novel patterns from stronger teachers. A critical open question is whether combining distillation and RLVR can synergistically overcome this ceiling—using distillation to first expand the reachable reasoning space, then applying RLVR to improve selection efficiency within that expanded space. Proposed Method: We propose a two-stage pipeline: (1) Distillation Bootstrap—fine-tune the base model on teacher-generated reasoning traces (e.g., from DeepSeek-R1 or o3) to expand pass@k coverage beyond the base model ceiling; (2) Coverage-Aware RLVR—apply RLVR with a modified reward that explicitly penalizes solutions already well-covered by the base model and rewards solutions in newly unlocked regions (identified via perplexity differential between base and distilled model). This steers RL exploration toward genuinely novel reasoning patterns rather than mere reranking. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks across Qwen2.5, LLaMA3, and Mistral families, measuring pass@k curves (k=1 to 256), coverage overlap with base model, and perplexity analysis. Ablations compare distill-only, RLVR-only, sequential distill+RLVR, and our coverage-aware variant.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Curiosity-Driven Exploration to Push RLVR Beyond Base Model Coverage Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR-trained LLMs are bounded by base model coverage—they cannot generate reasoning patterns not already latent in the base model. This fundamentally limits self-improvement. We hypothesize this occurs because standard RLVR only reinforces correct solutions the model already occasionally produces (high pass@k problems), never venturing into genuinely novel reasoning territory. Proposed Method: We introduce Novelty-Augmented RLVR (NA-RLVR), which adds an intrinsic curiosity reward that incentivizes generating reasoning chains with low perplexity under the RL-trained model but high perplexity under the frozen base model—explicitly rewarding deviation from base model distribution. This novelty reward is combined with the standard verifiable correctness reward, with a curriculum that gradually increases novelty weighting. To prevent reward hacking, novelty is measured at the reasoning-step level via a bank of base model perplexity scores over solution trajectories. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and geometry visual reasoning. Key metrics include pass@k for large k (coverage), pass@1 (efficiency), and a new 'coverage expansion ratio' measuring how much the trained model's support exceeds the base model's on hard problems. We compare against six standard RLVR baselines and distillation, directly testing whether curiosity-driven exploration breaks the coverage ceiling identified in the anchor paper.

title: Beyond Coverage Ceilings: Hybrid Distillation-RLVR Training to Genuinely Expand LLM Reasoning Boundaries
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR merely reshapes sampling distributions within base model coverage rather than introducing genuinely new reasoning patterns, while distillation can expand coverage by injecting teacher knowledge. However, naive distillation sacrifices the consistency improvements RLVR provides at low k. This gap motivates a hybrid approach that combines distillation's coverage expansion with RLVR's precision benefits. Phase 1 performs targeted distillation from a stronger teacher model, specifically focusing on problems where the student base model has zero pass@k coverage (identified via sampling), thereby injecting genuinely novel reasoning trajectories. Phase 2 applies RLVR starting from the distillation-augmented checkpoint, using a coverage-aware reward that explicitly incentivizes solutions to previously zero-coverage problems rather than over-optimizing already-covered problems. A coverage diversity bonus penalizes reward hacking on easy problems the base model already solves reliably. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks measuring pass@1, pass@k (large k), coverage expansion rate, and perplexity of novel solutions. Ablations isolate contributions of each phase. Baselines include pure RLVR, pure distillation, and sequential combinations without coverage-aware rewards.

title: Escape Velocity: Using Diversity-Driven RL to Break the Base Model Reasoning Ceiling
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR-trained LLMs remain bounded by their base model's reasoning coverage at large k, merely improving selection efficiency rather than discovering genuinely new reasoning patterns. This ceiling effect limits RL's potential for true capability expansion. Proposed Method: We introduce Diversity-Driven RLVR (D2-RLVR), which augments standard verifiable reward signals with an explicit reasoning-diversity bonus. Specifically, we maintain a rolling buffer of successful solution traces per problem and add an intrinsic reward term measuring edit-distance or semantic dissimilarity between new correct solutions and buffered ones. This incentivizes the policy to explore structurally novel reasoning paths rather than concentrating probability mass on already-discovered strategies. Additionally, we incorporate a 'novelty penalty' that discourages solutions semantically identical to base model high-probability outputs, explicitly pressuring the model away from the base model's support. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH, Codeforces, and visual reasoning benchmarks using the anchor paper's pass@k framework as primary metric. We track coverage expansion relative to base model across training steps, measure perplexity of generated solutions under the base model, and perform token-level analysis of novel reasoning patterns. Baselines include standard GRPO, PPO, and distillation. We hypothesize D2-RLVR will show pass@k curves that eventually exceed base model coverage.

title: Escape Velocity: Curriculum-Guided Multi-Turn Environment Interaction to Break the Base Model Ceiling in RLVR
description:
Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that current RLVR methods are bounded by the base model's latent reasoning capacity—they improve selection efficiency (pass@1) but cannot generate genuinely novel reasoning patterns absent from the base model's distribution. This ceiling fundamentally limits self-improvement. We hypothesize that the missing ingredient is sustained, grounded interaction with an external environment that provides out-of-distribution feedback signals, forcing the model to construct genuinely new reasoning traces.

Proposed Method: We design a multi-turn curriculum RL framework where the LLM acts as an agent in a structured mathematical proof environment (Lean 4). The agent iteratively proposes proof steps, receives verifier feedback (type errors, failed tactics), and must revise—creating trajectories that cannot be hallucinated from base model priors alone. A curriculum scheduler progressively introduces theorems requiring reasoning chains absent from pretraining data (verified via n-gram novelty scoring against pretraining corpora). We augment PPO with a 'novelty bonus' reward that explicitly incentivizes solutions with low base-model likelihood, counteracting mode collapse toward known patterns.

Experiments: (1) Replicate anchor paper's pass@k analysis on our trained models vs. base models and standard RLVR; (2) Measure coverage expansion on miniF2F and ProofNet benchmarks; (3) Perplexity analysis comparing solution traces against base model; (4) Ablations isolating curriculum vs. multi-turn vs. novelty bonus contributions; (5) Transfer evaluation on out-of-domain math benchmarks to test generalization of newly acquired reasoning patterns.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Curiosity-Driven Exploration in RLVR to Elicit Genuinely Novel Reasoning Patterns
description: Problem: The anchor paper demonstrates that RLVR merely reweights reasoning paths already latent in the base model, never genuinely expanding its capability frontier. The core failure is insufficient exploration—standard RLVR optimizes pass@1 greedily, collapsing toward high-probability base-model outputs rather than discovering structurally novel solution strategies. This encourages the policy to discover diverse, structurally distinct reasoning patterns beyond base-model modes. We further combine this with a replay buffer of 'frontier solutions'—high-novelty correct traces used to bootstrap subsequent training steps. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and a visual reasoning benchmark (MathVista). Using pass@k at large k (k=64,256) as the primary metric, we compare NA-RLVR against six baselines from the anchor paper plus distillation. Coverage analysis and perplexity relative to the base model quantify whether novel reasoning patterns genuinely emerge. We ablate novelty bonus weight and replay buffer size, and measure whether the base-model ceiling identified in the anchor paper is measurably lifted.

title: Escaping the Base Model Ceiling: Iterative Distillation-RL Cycles for Genuinely Novel Reasoning Acquisition

title: Beyond Coverage Ceilings: Iterative Distillation-RL Cycles to Genuinely Expand LLM Reasoning Boundaries
description:
Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reshuffles existing base model capabilities (higher pass@1 but lower pass@k ceiling), while distillation genuinely expands reasoning coverage by introducing teacher patterns. This raises a critical question: can we design a hybrid training paradigm that breaks the base model's coverage ceiling iteratively, rather than accepting it as a fixed upper bound?

Proposed Method: We introduce 'Distill-then-RL' (D-RL) cycles — an iterative framework where (1) a stronger teacher model generates novel reasoning traces not present in the student's current coverage, (2) these are distilled into the student to expand its latent reasoning space, and (3) RLVR is applied to consolidate and optimize the newly acquired patterns. Crucially, after each cycle, the expanded student becomes the new 'base,' and we measure whether pass@k ceilings genuinely increase across cycles. We also explore self-distillation variants where the model distills its own high-temperature diverse samples back into itself.

Experiments: (1) Track pass@k (large k) across D-RL cycles on MATH500, AIME, HumanEval, and visual reasoning benchmarks. (2) Coverage analysis via embedding clustering to verify new reasoning patterns emerge. (3) Ablations: RL-only vs distill-only vs D-RL cycles. (4) Compare against continual RLVR baselines to isolate genuine capability expansion.

title: Capability Distillation as a Bootstrap for RLVR: Unlocking Genuinely Novel Reasoning via Teacher-Student-RL Pipelines
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reshapes the base model's existing reasoning distribution (improving pass@1 at the cost of pass@k coverage), while distillation genuinely expands capabilities. Yet distillation requires a stronger teacher, and pure RLVR plateaus. Can we combine these insights to build a self-improving loop that actually generates novel reasoning patterns without an external oracle? Proposed Method: We introduce 'Distill-then-Explore' (DtE), a two-phase iterative pipeline. Phase 1: Use targeted distillation from a larger teacher to install qualitatively new solution strategies on a hard problem subset where the base model has zero pass@k coverage—creating a 'capability seed.' Phase 2: Apply RLVR starting from this distilled checkpoint, with an explicit diversity-promoting reward (penalizing solutions too similar to training demonstrations via embedding-based novelty bonuses) to explore beyond the teacher's patterns. We iterate these phases, using pass@k coverage growth as the stopping criterion. Experiments: Evaluate on MATH-500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and a novel spatial-reasoning benchmark. Track pass@k curves, solution cluster diversity (k-means over chain-of-thought embeddings), and out-of-distribution generalization to unseen problem types. Compare against pure RLVR, pure distillation, naive fine-tune+RLVR, and larger teacher baselines. Primary metric is genuine coverage expansion beyond the base model's support.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding Base Model Reasoning Boundaries via Diversity-Incentivized RLVR
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reweights existing base model reasoning patterns rather than discovering genuinely novel ones, as evidenced by base models dominating at large pass@k. This exposes a fundamental limitation: standard outcome-based rewards optimize for mode-seeking behavior, collapsing solution diversity rather than expanding it. Proposed Method: We introduce Coverage-Guided RLVR (CG-RLVR), which augments verifiable outcome rewards with an intrinsic diversity reward that incentivizes exploration of reasoning trajectories not already well-covered by the base model. Specifically, we maintain a trajectory embedding buffer and compute a novelty bonus based on cosine distance from base model high-probability regions in reasoning-step embedding space. We also add a 'boundary-crossing' reward that explicitly bonuses solutions whose intermediate reasoning steps have low base model likelihood but correct final answers, directly targeting the gap identified in the anchor paper. Experiments: We evaluate on MATH500, GSM8K, AIME, and HumanEval using pass@k (k=1,10,100) as primary metrics, comparing against base models, standard GRPO/PPO RLVR, and distillation baselines. We measure coverage expansion via unique solution clustering and perplexity shifts. We test on Qwen2.5-7B/32B and Llama-3.1-8B families. We hypothesize CG-RLVR will close the large-k gap between RLVR-trained and base models, demonstrating genuine reasoning boundary expansion.

title: Boundary-Aware RLVR: Dynamically Estimating and Expanding Base Model Coverage to Enable Genuine Reasoning Novelty
description: Problem: The anchor paper shows RLVR merely reshapes the sampling distribution within the base model's existing coverage rather than expanding it. This raises a critical question: can we design RLVR training signals that explicitly detect when a model is near its coverage boundary and push beyond it, rather than just improving selection efficiency within known patterns? Proposed Method: We introduce Boundary-Aware RLVR (BA-RLVR), which maintains a running estimate of base model coverage via pass@k probing on a held-out problem set throughout training. When coverage saturation is detected (plateau in pass@k delta), BA-RLVR switches to a 'boundary expansion' phase that injects distilled reasoning traces from a stronger teacher model—but only for problems where the base model has zero coverage—then resumes RL fine-tuning on these newly acquired patterns. This hybrid loop alternates between RL-driven consolidation and distillation-driven boundary expansion. Experiments: We benchmark on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and MathVista using pass@k (k=1,4,16,64,256) across Qwen2.5-7B/32B and LLaMA-3.1-8B base models. We compare against vanilla GRPO, PPO, and pure distillation baselines, measuring coverage growth curves, perplexity on novel patterns, and wall-clock compute efficiency, to verify that BA-RLVR uniquely expands rather than merely redistributes reasoning capability.

title: Boundary-Aware RLVR: Dynamically Estimating and Expanding the Base Model's Reasoning Coverage Ceiling
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR merely reorganizes existing base model capabilities rather than generating genuinely novel reasoning patterns, with the base model's pass@k coverage acting as an implicit ceiling. However, no method exists to dynamically estimate this coverage boundary during training and use it to guide exploration toward regions where the base model consistently fails. Proposed Method: We introduce Boundary-Aware RLVR (BA-RLVR), which maintains a running estimate of the base model's problem-level coverage boundary using lightweight Monte Carlo sampling (moderate k~50) throughout training. Problems where the base model already achieves high coverage receive reduced reward shaping, redirecting training signal toward 'coverage-dark' problems where the base model consistently fails across all samples. For these hard problems, we augment RL exploration with targeted distillation micro-batches from a stronger teacher model, creating a hybrid objective that uses distillation precisely where RL alone cannot escape the base model ceiling. Experiments: We evaluate BA-RLVR on MATH500, AIME, LiveCodeBench, and visual reasoning benchmarks using both pass@1 and pass@k (k up to 256). Ablations isolate (1) boundary estimation frequency, (2) distillation injection threshold, and (3) different base models. We measure whether BA-RLVR shifts the coverage ceiling upward beyond the base model, directly testing whether the hybrid approach enables genuinely novel reasoning acquisition.

title: Coverage-Guided Reward Shaping: Expanding Reasoning Boundaries Beyond Base Model Ceilings in RLVR
description: Problem: The anchor paper reveals that RLVR-trained models are bounded by the base model's reasoning coverage—they increase pass@1 but reduce pass@k diversity, never exceeding base model coverage at large k. This suggests current RLVR reward signals (binary correct/incorrect) cause mode-seeking behavior that collapses solution diversity rather than expanding it.
